strengths: Principled adaptation of cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) to protein language models (pLMs), moving beyond isolated layerwise sparse autoencoders to capture inter-layer computational pathways.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning two distinct biologically relevant tasks: protein family classification on Swiss-Prot and fitness prediction across 12 Deep Mutational Scanning (DMS) assays from ProteinGym.

Convincing biological case studies (protein kinase domain, NADP+ binding domain, and GB1 stability/affinity mutations) demonstrating that discovered circuits map directly to known biochemical motifs such as the catalytic HRD motif, ATP-binding pocket, Rossmann fold, and hydrophobic core packing.

Practical utility demonstrated via circuit-guided activation steering, showing higher fitness scores on in silico DMS evaluations compared to per-layer transcoders (PLTs), Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), and random baselines.
Extensive appendix detailing architectural choices, replacement model variants (direct, sequential, full replacement), steering ablations, and a dedicated interactive visualization platform.
weaknesses: Experiments are restricted entirely to ESM2-8M (6 layers, d_model = 320). As noted in the limitations, CLT decoder parameters scale with O(L^2), which creates practical barriers to scaling to standard production pLMs (e.g., ESM2-650M or ESM2-3B). Testing on at least one intermediate scale model (e.g., ESM2-35M or 150M) would significantly strengthen the empirical findings.

The steering validation relies on a surrogate CNN evaluation model trained on 90% of the experimental DMS data rather than wet-lab experimental testing or strictly orthogonal structural/functional assays. While standard for in silico evaluation, potential surrogate bias should be addressed more explicitly.

The comparison in Table 1 uses the 'direct' replacement model for ProtoMech but the 'sequential' model for PLT (due to structural differences in cross-layer connectivity). While Appendix Table 4 provides the apples-to-apples sequential vs. sequential comparison (where ProtoMech still wins in 61% of cases), this distinction and its implications should be highlighted more clearly in the main text.

The circuit tracing is restricted to the MLP subnetwork, with attention outputs held fixed to ground-truth ESM2 values in the primary experiments because full replacement incurs compounding reconstruction errors. This leaves attention-mediated circuit components unmodeled.

strengths: First application of cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) to protein language models, moving beyond isolated representational factorizations (SAEs) toward compositional, multi-layer circuit tracing.
The framework is thorough and end-to-end, integrating CLT training, attribution-based circuit discovery, functional sequence steering, and an interactive open-source visualization tool.

ProtoMech substantially outperforms per-layer transcoders (PLTs) across both protein family classification and fitness prediction tasks, retaining ~74-79% of original performance with under 1% of the latent space.

Strong qualitative validation aligning internal circuit pathways with established biochemical and structural mechanisms (e.g., arginine detection feeding into the HRD catalytic loop and ATP-binding sites in kinases, Rossmann fold detection in NADP+ binding, and core hydrophobic stabilization in GB1 mutants).
Comprehensive appendix and ablations detailing different replacement model configurations (direct, sequential, full replacement) and addressing error propagation dynamics.
weaknesses: Evaluated exclusively on the smallest ESM2 variant (ESM2-8M, 6 layers). Because CLT decoder parameters scale quadratically with depth ($O(L^2)$), computational feasibility and scaling behavior on standard medium-to-large pLMs (e.g., ESM2-650M or ESM2-3B) remain unproven.

Evaluation of functional sequence steering relies entirely on an in-silico CNN surrogate model trained on DMS data rather than wet-lab experimental validation or orthogonal biophysical simulations (e.g., Rosetta or FoldX $\Delta\Delta G$), introducing potential surrogate model bias.

The replacement model does not fully replace attention computations: in both the direct and sequential replacement setups used for primary results, attention outputs are frozen to ground-truth ESM2 values, meaning the recovered circuits isolate MLP computations rather than tracing complete self-contained transformer circuits.

strengths: First application of cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) to protein language models (ESM2), advancing beyond single-layer sparse autoencoders (SAEs) toward compositional, multi-layer circuit tracing in biology.

Comprehensive downstream task coverage, evaluating both protein family classification across Swiss-Prot/InterPro families and fitness prediction across 12 ProteinGym deep mutational scanning (DMS) assays.

In-depth qualitative case studies (kinase catalytic HRD motif, NADP+ binding/Rossmann fold, and GB1 W43 core stability) that convincingly demonstrate latent features aligning with known biophysical and structural properties.
Extensive implementation and benchmarking of multiple replacement model paradigms (direct, sequential, and full replacement), openly discussing error compounding in full replacement settings.
Development of an interactive visualization interface supporting multi-layer circuit exploration, virtual weights, and sequence alignment overlays.
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted entirely to ESM2-8M (6 layers, d_model=320). Because modern practical pLM applications rely on models orders of magnitude larger (e.g., ESM2-650M or ESM2-3B) and CLTs scale with O(L^2) decoder matrices (requiring 28M parameters to transcode an 8M model), the method's feasibility and utility on realistic models remain unproven.

Circular in silico steering evaluation: The fitness of generated variants is scored using a 1D-CNN trained on 90% of the DMS assay, which uses the exact same architecture and training procedure as the CNN probes used during circuit discovery. Evaluating steered variants on an internal surrogate model rather than an independent biophysical oracle (e.g., Rosetta, FoldX, molecular dynamics) or experimental validation risks measuring surrogate overfitting rather than true biological fitness.

Asymmetric baseline comparison in steering: For steering (Table 1), ProtoMech uses the 'direct replacement model' (which injects ground-truth residual activations at intermediate layers), whereas PLT uses the 'sequential replacement model' where errors compound across layers. This creates an uneven comparison that favors ProtoMech.

Incomplete circuit coverage due to frozen attention: ProtoMech only models MLP transformations while relying on ground-truth attention outputs (in sequential and direct modes). When evaluating true end-to-end full replacement (where attention heads receive transcoded inputs), performance drops steeply (Figures 5 and 7), showing that the discovered circuits are not yet faithful, autonomous representations of the network's end-to-end computation.

Marginal steering performance gains over PLT: On several DMS datasets in Table 1 (such as SPG1 and GFP), PLT actually achieves higher mean or maximum fitness scores than ProtoMech, making the claim of consistent superiority over per-layer transcoders overstated.

strengths: First principled application of cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) to protein language models (pLMs), successfully bridging the gap between isolated representation decomposition (SAEs) and end-to-end computational circuit discovery in biology.

Thorough empirical investigation of replacement model formulations (direct, sequential, and full replacement), detailing how compounding reconstruction errors affect circuit discovery and providing practical guidelines for interpreting MLPs in transformers.

Extensive quantitative evaluation across two biologically meaningful domains: protein family classification (InterPro) and multiple mutational scanning fitness landscapes (ProteinGym), demonstrating that circuits using <1% of the latent space retain ~75-80% of model performance.

Functional validation through activation steering, showing that targeted circuit clamping consistently outperforms dense steering baselines (Contrastive Activation Addition), per-layer transcoders (PLTs), and even black-box optimizers (PEX, GGS) under surrogate fitness evaluations.

Convincing biological case studies (protein kinase HRD motif and ATP binding, NADP+ binding domain and Rossmann folds, and GB1 stability/interface mutations) demonstrating mechanistic and biochemical interpretability.

Thoughtful treatment of the quadratic computational complexity O(L^2) of CLTs via the proposed 'windowed' CLT architecture, validated empirically on ESM2-35M with significant parameter and training time savings.
weaknesses: Experiments are restricted to small model scales (ESM2-8M and ESM2-35M), whereas state-of-the-art pLM applications predominantly rely on ESM2-650M or ESM2-3B; representations and circuit behavior may exhibit qualitative shifts at scale.

Circuit tracing isolates MLP layers by freezing ground-truth attention outputs (in sequential replacement) or using ground-truth residual states (in direct replacement), leaving attention head computations as an unmodeled black box and suffering notable performance degradation under fully autonomous replacement.

Steering validation relies exclusively on in-silico CNN surrogate models trained on the DMS datasets rather than biophysical simulations (e.g., Rosetta/MD) or wet-lab experimental validation, which poses potential risks of evaluation model exploitation/overfitting.

Circuit extraction employs a greedy gradient-based attribution heuristic that scores latent features individually, which may overlook non-linear polysemantic interactions or multi-latent synergistic logic.

strengths: Principled step forward for mechanistic interpretability in biology: The paper successfully transitions from static feature factorization (standard SAEs) to functional circuit tracing in protein language models using Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs), capturing inter-layer computational dependencies that isolated layerwise transcoders (PLTs) miss.

Strong empirical recovery and compression: On both protein family classification (InterPro) and fitness landscape modeling (ProteinGym DMS benchmarks), ProtoMech replacement models recover 82–89% of native ESM2 performance, and discovered circuits retain over 74–79% accuracy while utilizing less than 1% of the latent space.

Convincing biological groundedness: Case studies on protein kinase catalytic motifs (HRD loop, G-loop, ATP binding pocket), NADP+ binding domains (Rossmann fold), and GB1 mutational sensitivity (W43 hydrophobic packing and A24W/W43Q mutations) clearly illustrate that the extracted cross-layer latent pathways correspond to genuine biophysical and evolutionary mechanisms.

Practical architectural innovation for scalability: The paper introduces 'windowed CLTs' to mitigate the quadratic O(L^2) decoder scaling problem, demonstrating on ESM2-35M that a 4-layer window cuts parameter count by 40% and speeds up training by 1.75x while retaining 82% performance.

Comprehensive experimental execution and tooling: The inclusion of an interactive circuit exploration tool, clear ablations across replacement strategies (direct, sequential, full), and open-source release provide valuable infrastructure for the computational biology community.
weaknesses: Evaluations are limited to small pLM scales: The study focuses primarily on ESM2-8M, with supplementary scaling up to ESM2-35M. Modern state-of-the-art protein design and property prediction pipelines rely on ESM2-650M or ESM2-3B. Although the authors provide parameter/time projections in Table 10, empirical validation at larger scales (>=150M) remains unproven.

Steering validation relies on an in-silico CNN proxy: The fitness evaluation of steered sequences is performed using a CNN surrogate trained on DMS data with the same architecture and training routine as the circuit discovery probe. While standard in computational benchmarks, this creates potential risk of proxy bias or co-adaptation, and lacking orthogonal biophysical validation (e.g., Rosetta ddG, molecular dynamics, or experimental assay data) weakens the claim of high-fitness design.

Asymmetric baseline comparison in main steering results: As noted in Appendix C.2 and Table 1, ProtoMech steering results utilize the 'direct' replacement model while the PLT baseline is restricted to the 'sequential' model (as direct replacement cannot be applied to PLTs). Although Appendix Table 6 shows sequential ProtoMech still outperforms PLT in 61% of cases, presenting the direct vs. sequential comparison in the main text gives ProtoMech an architectural advantage not available to the baseline.

Probe dependence in circuit definition: Anchoring circuit tracing to downstream supervised probes (logistic regression and CNN) means the identified circuits are conditioned on the probe's inductive biases and target tasks rather than the pre-trained model's intrinsic masked-language-modeling head.

strengths: Principled adaptation of cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) to protein language models (pLMs), moving beyond the static representational factorization of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) and per-layer transcoders (PLTs) toward compositional, layer-to-layer circuit discovery.

Comprehensive empirical validation across diverse biological benchmarks, including protein family classification on Swiss-Prot/InterPro and fitness prediction across 12 Deep Mutational Scanning (DMS) datasets from ProteinGym.

Discovered circuits achieve substantial compression (retaining 74–79% of original model performance with <1% of the latent space) and demonstrate practical utility in steering sequences toward higher fitness, outperforming Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), PLTs, ESM2 logits, and black-box optimization baselines (PEX, GGS).

Thorough qualitative analysis linking identified circuit latents and connections directly to established biochemical motifs (e.g., HRD catalytic loop and G-loop in kinases, Rossmann fold in NADP+ binding, and hydrophobic packing involving W43 in GB1).

Thoughtful analysis of scalability bottlenecks: the paper evaluates ESM2-35M, explores the quadratic parameter scaling of full CLTs, and proposes a windowed CLT variant that substantially cuts parameters and training time while preserving most performance.
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted to small pLM checkpoints (ESM2-8M and ESM2-35M). While parameter scaling challenges are documented and windowed CLTs are tested on ESM2-35M, it remains unproven whether the method scales effectively to widely deployed, high-capacity models (e.g., ESM2-650M or 3B) where complex biological capabilities most clearly emerge.

Reliance on hybrid/sequential replacement rather than autonomous full replacement: as shown in Figure 5 and Appendix C, fully unrolling transcoders across depth without conditioning on base attention representations causes significant performance degradation due to compounding reconstruction errors.

Steering validation is conducted entirely in-silico using a surrogate CNN evaluation model trained on local DMS data rather than wet-lab experimental confirmation, which introduces potential surrogate model bias into the reported sequence fitness gains.

Core algorithmic novelty is relatively incremental, primarily transferring recent mechanistic interpretability frameworks from natural language (e.g., Ameisen et al., 2025; Dunefsky et al., 2024) to the protein domain rather than introducing fundamentally new circuit-discovery formulations.
